text: This linear functional reads the coefficient of the basis symbol g in R[G], the coefficient operation used in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Despite the name monoid algebra, these declarations need only an arbitrary label type G: they use its free module and diagonal coalgebra, without multiplication on labels. The output is the actual scalar coefficient. Checks pass: [monoidCoeff_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L133), [tensorComponent_monoidCoeff_comul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L177).
The functional evaluates to the stored coefficient.
Coefficient contraction agrees with diagonal comultiplication.

The coefficient functional at g returns exactly the g-coordinate of the finitely supported expression representing an element of R[G]. This connects the bundled linear map with the coefficients in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). It works over a commutative semiring and an arbitrary label type; no ordering, multiplication or finite cardinality of the labels is assumed. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L161), [tensorComponent_monoidCoeff_comul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L177).
Tensor coefficients scale the vector by these same scalar coefficients.
The same coefficient functional extracts the expected diagonal coproduct term.

An element of V⊗R[G] is identified with its finitely supported family of V-valued coefficients, as used in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The inverse sends a single coefficient v at g to v⊗[g]. This is an actual linear equivalence of free-coefficient tensor expressions; it requires neither a basis of V nor finitely many labels. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L161), [tensorCoeffEquiv_symm_single](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L170).
The forward map has the expected coefficient formula on pure tensors.
The inverse takes a single coefficient to its basis tensor.

The g-coordinate of the tensor coefficient family is obtained by applying the g-coefficient functional to the R[G] factor and identifying V⊗R with V. This is the basis-free coefficient extraction in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The formula compares two actual linear constructions, so it applies to arbitrary tensors, not just a chosen pure-tensor decomposition. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L161), [tensorCoeffEquiv_symm_single](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L170).
Pure tensors give scalar coefficient times vector.
The inverse recovers a basis tensor from its single coefficient.

The coefficients of v⊗a are the vectors a_g v. This explicitly computes the tensor-coordinate identification underlying [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The result is a finitely supported family because a has finite support; multiplication of a coefficient by v is scalar multiplication, and zero coefficients may reduce the support further. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L150), [tensorCoeffEquiv_symm_single](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L170).
Coordinate evaluation agrees with contraction by the coefficient functional.
A single nonzero coordinate recovers the corresponding basis tensor.

The inverse coefficient map sends the family with vector v at label g and zero elsewhere to v⊗[g], where [g] is the monoid-algebra symbol with coefficient 1. This is the reconstruction step used in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The label need not have a multiplication law, and the formula remains valid when v is zero. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_tmul](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L161), [coact_eq_symm_weightDecomposition](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L244).
Forward coefficient extraction recovers this single-coordinate family.
The inverse reconstructs an actual coaction from its weight coefficients.

Contracting the second factor of the coproduct at label g yields a_g[g], since each basis symbol has coproduct [g]⊗[g]. This is the diagonal-coalgebra coefficient calculation behind [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Coefficients are not divided or normalized: the result follows by linearity from the group-like basis symbols over the stated commutative semiring. Checks pass: [tensorComponent_monoidCoeff_comul_lTensor](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L192), [monoidCoeff_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L133).
The contraction formula also holds with an additional vector tensor factor.
The coefficient used is exactly the g-coordinate of the original element.

The g-weight projection extracts the g-coefficient of the coaction ρ(v). Coassociativity makes these operators idempotent and makes distinct projections annihilate one another, exactly the coefficient argument in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Thus projection means an algebraic component map, not an orthogonal projection for an inner product; no inner product is present. Checks pass: [weightProj_weightProj_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L318), [weightProj_weightProj_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L325).
Each component map is idempotent.
Distinct component maps compose to zero.

This equation identifies the weight projection with contraction of the coaction by the g-coefficient functional. It therefore extracts the vector multiplying [g] in the finite expansion of ρ(v), as in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The operation is intrinsic to the supplied coaction and chosen label, without selecting a basis of V. Checks pass: [weightDecomposition_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L239), [weightProj_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L373).
The same projection is the g-coordinate of the packaged decomposition.
Its output has precisely the corresponding diagonal coaction.

The construction sends v to the finitely supported coefficient family of its coaction. As in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246), those coefficients are its weight components and their sum recovers v. Finite support is asserted separately for each vector; this definition does not assert that the entire module has only finitely many nonzero weight spaces. Checks pass: [weightDecomposition_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L239), [weightDecomposition_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L284).
Each stored component is the corresponding weight projection.
The finite sum of components recovers the original vector.

The g-entry of the stored finite-support decomposition equals the g-weight projection of v. Both sides contract the same coaction coefficient, matching the construction in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). This equation exposes how the abstract family encodes its individual components; a zero entry simply means that this vector has no component at that label. Checks pass: [weightProj_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L221), [weightDecomposition_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L284).
The projection is contraction by the stated coefficient functional.
The family of these entries reconstructs the vector by summation.

The coaction is recovered by converting its finite family of weight coefficients back into a tensor. This is the expansion ρ(v)=Σv_g⊗[g] used in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The identity follows from the inverse tensor-coordinate equivalence, so the decomposition records the actual coaction, rather than merely some family whose vectors sum to v. Checks pass: [tensorCoeffEquiv_symm_single](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L170), [weightDecomposition_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L239).
Each individual coefficient reconstructs its labelled basis tensor.
The stored coefficients are the actual weight projections.

The finite sum of all weight components equals the original vector. The counit sends every group-like basis symbol [g] to 1, so applying the counit to the coaction adds its coefficients; the comodule counit law then returns v. This is exactly the second equality in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246), with no infinite summation or convergence convention. Checks pass: [weightDecomposition_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L239), [iSup_weightSpace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L398).
The summands are the individual weight projections.
These actual finite decompositions show that the weight spaces span the module.

Extracting the g-component twice gives the same result as extracting it once. Coassociativity and the diagonal coproduct [g]↦[g]⊗[g] prove this idempotence, following [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). This is an algebraic projection identity over a commutative semiring; it does not rely on division, eigenvalue separation or an inner product. Checks pass: [weightProj_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L373), [weightProj_of_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L362).
The first projection already lands in its weight space.
Projection acts identically on vectors in that weight space.

For different labels h and g, extracting the h-component of a g-component gives zero. The distinct coefficient functionals annihilate the corresponding diagonal coproduct term, as in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Here orthogonal means that the projections compose to zero; it expresses separation of formal weight labels, rather than orthogonality for a bilinear form. Checks pass: [weightProj_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L373), [weightProj_of_mem_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L367).
The g-component lies in the g-weight space.
Projection at another label kills every vector in that weight space.

The g-weight space consists of vectors satisfying ρ(v)=v⊗[g], the coaction characterization in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Linearity makes this a submodule. The definition retains the formal label g and works even when different characters cannot be distinguished by base-field points; it uses the full coaction, not pointwise eigenvalues or differentiated Lie eigenvalues. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L356), [weightProj_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L373).
Membership is exactly the stated coaction equation.
The coefficient projection really lands in this submodule.

Membership in the g-weight submodule is equivalent to the explicit coaction equation v↦v⊗[g]. This exposes the same weight condition as [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246), with [g] the basis symbol carrying coefficient 1. The equivalence is definitional: no existence of rational points, smoothness, or distinct scalar eigenvalues is required. Checks pass: [weightProj_of_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L362), [weightProj_of_mem_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L367).
A vector satisfying this equation is fixed by its own projection.
The same equation forces all differently labelled projections to vanish.

A vector already in the g-weight space is fixed by its g-projection, because the coefficient of [g] in v⊗[g] is v. This is the coefficient calculation in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The conclusion uses the actual coaction membership hypothesis and the basis coefficient 1, so it needs no division or nonzero-eigenvalue assumption. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L356), [weightProj_weightProj_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L318).
Membership supplies the exact diagonal coaction used in the calculation.
The resulting identity specializes to the idempotence of the projection.

A vector of weight g has zero projection at every different label h, since the h-coefficient of v⊗[g] vanishes. This is the coefficient separation used in [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The inequality concerns the labels themselves; no assertion about distinct evaluations of characters at field-valued points is involved. Checks pass: [mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L356), [weightProj_weightProj_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L325).
The weight hypothesis supplies v⊗[g] as the full coaction.
The formula yields annihilation of distinct component projections.

Every extracted g-component has coaction v_g⊗[g], so it belongs to the g-weight space. Coassociativity makes its other components zero and its own component unchanged; reconstruction of the coaction gives the result. This is the central first equality of [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246), proved here over a commutative semiring without a finite-dimensionality assumption. Checks pass: [weightProj_weightProj_self](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L318), [weightProj_weightProj_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L325).
The extracted vector retains its own component.
All other components vanish, permitting reconstruction of its diagonal coaction.

The weight submodules span V because every vector is the finite sum of its weight projections, each lying in its corresponding weight space. This is the spanning conclusion of [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The supremum denotes the submodule generated by all weight spaces; this statement alone asserts spanning, not uniqueness of a decomposition. Checks pass: [weightDecomposition_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L284), [weightProj_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L373).
Each vector is an actual finite sum of components.
Every summand lies in its stated weight submodule.

Each weight space meets the submodule generated by all the other weight spaces only at zero: its projection fixes the former and kills the latter. This is the independence argument behind [Milne, Theorem 12.12 proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Over semirings, this lattice-theoretic assertion alone need not imply uniqueness of direct-sum expressions; the separate reconstruction proof uses the actual projections. Checks pass: [weightProj_of_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L362), [weightProj_of_mem_of_ne](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L367).
The chosen projection fixes its own weight space.
It kills each other weight space and hence their generated submodule.

A linear map preserving every labelled weight space commutes with the coactions: decompose a vector into its finitely many weight components and check the diagonal coaction on each. This implements the graded-map direction of [Milne, Remark 12.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The supplied map need not be injective, surjective or an equivalence. Checks pass: [ofMapWeightSpace_toLinearMap](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L508), [map_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L533).
The constructed comodule morphism has exactly the supplied linear map.
Actual comodule morphisms satisfy the converse weight-preservation property.

The comodule morphism constructed from a weight-preserving linear map has precisely that original linear map as its underlying function. The added field is a proof of coaction compatibility, not a replacement operation. This matches the grading interpretation in [Milne, Remark 12.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246), with preservation required for every formal weight label. Checks pass: [map_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L533), [map_weightProj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L514).
Comodule morphisms preserve the declared weight spaces.
The resulting morphism commutes with all coefficient projections.

A comodule morphism commutes with extracting each weight component: applying the map before or after the g-projection gives the same vector. Coaction compatibility and linear coefficient contraction prove this, matching the graded-map interpretation of [Milne, Remark 12.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). No injectivity, surjectivity or finite-dimensionality of either module is assumed. Checks pass: [map_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L533), [weightProj_apply](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L221).
The morphism carries each labelled weight space into the corresponding one.
Each projection is explicitly the coefficient contraction used in the intertwining proof.

A real/complex scalar field becomes a real inner-product space using Re(conj(x)y). For complex numbers this is the ordinary dot product of their two real coordinates; for real numbers it is multiplication. The existing norm is retained, so the construction changes which scalars act without changing lengths or distances. Compared with [Axler Chapter 4, §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L996).

The scalar field itself has inner product ⟨x,y⟩=conj(x)y and its usual norm. This is the one-dimensional real or complex example, conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in the second. Axler’s convention conjugates the second argument instead; swapping arguments reconciles the formulas without changing the norm. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L915).

The complex numbers are viewed here as a real inner-product space, with ⟨w,z⟩=Re(z conj(w)). For w=a+bi, z=c+di it is ac+bd, giving the Euclidean norm on the plane. It differs from the complex-valued inner product: 1 and i are orthogonal over the reals, although their complex inner product is nonzero. Compared with [Axler Chapter 4, §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L987).

The real inner product is packaged as a bilinear map: fixing either argument gives a real-linear function. Evaluating the package at two vectors returns the original inner product, and swapping arguments leaves it unchanged. The hypotheses allow a seminorm, so bilinearity does not imply that the form is nondegenerate. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L146).

This packages the inner product as a map conjugate-linear in the first argument and linear in the second. Thus multiplying the first vector by i multiplies the value by −i in the complex case. For real scalars conjugation is trivial and the same construction is bilinear; degeneracy is allowed. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L132).

This defines a real-valued pairing by taking the real part of an existing real/complex inner product. The vectors themselves stay unchanged; this is not projection onto a real subspace. The definition packages just the new operation, while the following construction supplies its real inner-product-space structure and preserves the original seminorm. Compared with [Axler Chapter 4, §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L944).

Restricting scalars to the reals and taking Re⟨x,y⟩ gives a real inner-product-space structure on the same vectors with the same seminorm. Complex orthogonality implies real orthogonality, but the converse can fail. Positive definiteness and completeness are not required; the construction also applies when the original form has nonzero null vectors. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L956).

A vector has zero self-inner-product exactly when it is zero. Here the ambient space has a genuine norm, whose zero value forces the zero vector; this stronger hypothesis is essential. The result would fail for a merely seminormed space with a degenerate inner product, even though many surrounding formulas remain valid there. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L316).

Cauchy–Schwarz bounds the modulus of the inner product by the product of the two seminorms. It holds even for degenerate forms and needs neither completeness nor finite dimension. If either vector has zero seminorm, the inner product vanishes; the usual equality criterion involving linear dependence is not part of this statement. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L455).

Two vectors are equal if their inner products with every test vector in the first argument agree. Testing with their difference makes its self-inner-product zero. The genuine-norm hypothesis then gives equality; with a degenerate seminorm, such tests would determine vectors only up to a null vector. No finite-dimensional basis is assumed. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L324).

Two vectors are equal if their inner products against every test vector in the second argument agree. Taking the test vector to be their difference reduces this to positive definiteness. A genuine norm is required; the result does not hold for arbitrary degenerate forms, and it needs neither completeness nor finite dimension. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L330).

The squared seminorm of x+y expands to ‖x‖²+2Re⟨x,y⟩+‖y‖². Taking the real part is essential over complex scalars: the two cross terms are conjugates. All terms in this equality are real numbers, and the formula holds for degenerate inner products without assuming orthogonality or completeness. Compared with [Axler Theorem 6.17](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L402).

The squared seminorm of x−y is ‖x‖²−2Re⟨x,y⟩+‖y‖². Subtraction is ordinary subtraction in the real numbers, not natural-number truncation; the cross term can have either sign. The identity applies to complex as well as real spaces, including degenerate forms, without an orthogonality assumption. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L430).

Taking an inner product with a finite sum in the second argument equals the sum of the inner products. The sum runs over the supplied finite set, even if the ambient index type is infinite; the empty sum is zero. This is finite additivity, with no convergence or completeness hypothesis. Compared with [Axler Theorem 6.6](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L164).

An inner product with a finite sum in its first argument expands as the sum of the separate inner products. Conjugate-linearity still includes ordinary additivity, so no conjugation of the summands is introduced. The index set may be empty, and no infinite-series convergence or completeness assumption is involved. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L159).

Scaling the first vector multiplies the inner product by the conjugate of the scalar. Over the complex numbers, scaling by i therefore multiplies the result by −i; over the reals it is ordinary homogeneity. This follows Mathlib’s first-conjugate convention, opposite to Axler’s first-linear convention, and includes zero scalars and degenerate spaces. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L107).

Scaling the second vector multiplies the inner product by the scalar itself, without conjugation. Thus the second argument is linear even for complex scalars, while the first is conjugate-linear. This is the opposite slot convention from Axler’s text. Zero scalars and degenerate seminormed spaces are allowed; no division is used. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L117).

A real inner product is unchanged when its arguments are swapped. This remains true for a positive semidefinite form on a seminormed space, so positive definiteness is unnecessary. The scalar field matters: over the complex numbers the corresponding identity includes conjugation, and swapping arguments need not preserve the value itself. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L61).

The existing seminorm equals the nonnegative square root of Re⟨x,x⟩. The diagonal is real and nonnegative, so this formula agrees with the usual inner-product norm and never invokes Lean’s value for square roots of negative inputs. It does not imply that zero seminorm forces a zero vector. Compared with [Clément–Martin §4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.03618) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L379).

The self-inner-product equals the square of the seminorm embedded into the scalar field. Although the equality is scalar-valued, its right side lies on the real axis, so the diagonal has zero imaginary part. The cast is ordinary real-scalar inclusion; the identity remains valid for nonzero vectors of zero seminorm. Compared with [Axler §6A](https://linear.axler.net/LADR4e.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/Basic.lean#L212).

Over any characteristic-zero field, every vector in V(m)⊗V(n) is uniquely a sum from the explicitly generated summands V(m+n−2k), for 0≤k≤min(m,n). This is a decomposition of representations, not just their characters. The index bound prevents natural-number subtraction from truncating. The computed family includes V(1)⊗V(1)=V(2)⊕V(0), with summand dimensions three and one. See [Etingof, Theorem9.18, p.57](https://math.mit.edu/~etingof/lnlg.pdf) and [the explicit construction](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/Algebra/Lie/Sl2/ClebschGordan.lean#L92).
